title: Grateful Dead Live at Curtis Hixon Convention Hall on 1973-12-18
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Stunning soundboard transfer of the Dec‑18 1973 Tampa show – crystal‑clear audio captures a high‑energy set highlighted by an epic Weather Report Suite → Dark Star → Eyes → Wharf Rat sequence.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑remastered soundboard tape delivers breathtaking clarity and brilliance, with only a brief AUD patch noted. Musically the concert is in top form: Jerry’s soaring lead work, Keith’s piano dominance, Phil’s booming bass and Bill’s tight drumming drive a second‑set marathon that many fans call one of 1973’s finest, especially the Weather Report Suite/Dark Star/Eyes/Wharf Rat suite.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 five‑star reviews uniformly praise both performance and sound quality; the show is rated as exceptional and the recording as excellent, yielding a high combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, brilliant clarity with superb low‑end definition; occasional short AUD patch around 14:20 and minor vocal “hollow” character noted by a few reviewers, but overall flawless.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Smooth transitions throughout, especially Eyes → Wharf Rat; the second‑set suite Weather Report Suite → Dark Star → Drums → Eyes → Wharf Rat is highlighted as a seamless, jazzy journey.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his confident, soaring lead work, slide‑like tone, and some of the best playing of the year; described as ‘dialed in’ and ‘captain trips’ material.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass highlighted as “slapping away,” jazzy, prominent in the mix, and a key driver of the Weather Report Suite and Dark Star jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Solid rhythm guitar and vocals noted; occasional comments about his guitar being low in the mix but overall supportive of Jerry’s leads.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's piano/organ work described as front‑and‑center, brilliant, jazzy, and a major contributor to the show’s magic, especially during GSET and the second‑set suite.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill (drummer) commended for steady, clicking beats and tight drumming that fuels the jams; his transition into Dark Star praised.
